findings.message: The `stub` field is written as the JSON string `"false"` rather than the boolean `false` in `_security_lens_write_result` (both at the top level and inside `.data`); any jq consumer branching on `.stub` as a boolean (e.g. `if .stub then … end`) will receive a truthy value from the non-empty string, silently inverting the intended semantics — tests using `jq -r` do not catch this because `-r` renders both `false` and `"false"` as the output string `false`.

The `emit_event` call on the `resolve_tier` failure path hardcodes `"router_rc=2"` as a literal key-value string rather than referencing the `$router_rc` variable (which is `0` at that point in the function); consumers that parse `router_rc` as a diagnostic integer will see a sentinel value that conflates tier-resolution failure with a router exit-code-2 failure.

The `emit_event` on the `resolve_tier` fatal path does not include `result_contract=2`, while the normal-pass and router-fatal paths both emit that field; downstream consumers asserting that every `plugin.result` event from this plugin carries `result_contract=2` will see an inconsistent event on the tier-resolution failure branch.

The JSON-validity cross-check at line ~1492 validates `ZBUILD_STATE_FILE` even when `ZBUILD_STATE_DIR` is also set and will override it in the assignment below; the validated file is never actually used in that scenario, so a corrupt ambient `ZBUILD_STATE_FILE` causes a hard error even though it has no effect on the chosen `state_file` path — this is intentional per the comment but is a fail-closed behaviour that will surprise callers who set both variables.

`_security_lens_write_result` forks `date -u` as a subprocess on every invocation; the function is now called on all exit paths (pass, error, interrupt, resolve_tier failure), so error paths that previously paid zero forking cost now pay one extra process fork each — negligible for a once-per-run plugin but a regression relative to the prior code.

`findings_json` is embedded twice in every result artifact (top-level `.findings` and `.data.findings`) for backward compatibility; with `max_findings: 50` this doubles the JSON payload that `jq` must serialize and `atomic_write` must flush to disk on every run, increasing output size linearly with finding count.

`printf '%s' "$findings_json" | jq 'length'` spawns two subprocesses (printf + jq) to compute a count that could be obtained with a single here-string fork (`jq 'length' <<< "$findings_json"`); the SIGPIPE risk is absent since jq reads all input, but the extra fork is unnecessary.

Cross-check validates ZBUILD_STATE_FILE against --issue but when both ZBUILD_STATE_FILE and ZBUILD_STATE_DIR are set, ZBUILD_STATE_DIR wins for the actual state source at line ~1695 — the cross-check passes against a file that is never used, leaving the state derived from ZBUILD_STATE_DIR entirely unvalidated and creating a bypass path: an adversary who can set both vars presents a legitimate ZBUILD_STATE_FILE to satisfy the check while pointing ZBUILD_STATE_DIR at an attacker-controlled directory.

_sl_interrupted is set to 1 by the TERM/INT trap, but the only place it is checked is on the router_rc==130 branch; if a signal arrives in the window between trap registration and the route_to_model subshell launching, and the subshell subsequently completes with rc=0, the interrupted artifact written by the handler is silently overwritten by the normal pass path, causing an interrupted security review to be reported as verdict=pass.

stub field is emitted as JSON string "false" rather than boolean false; downstream consumers that test (.stub == false) in jq or strict JSON parsers that distinguish types will misread the value as truthy, silently treating a real artifact as a stub — tests mask the regression by using jq -r which renders both as the same output string.

SPEC-14 assertion (grep -cE '"[^"$]*\.(json|md)"') only matches quoted literals that contain no $ character, so it silently passes for the hardcoded basename in '$ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR/security-findings.json' — the manifest-undeclared basename security-findings.json embedded in the interpolated string is never flagged, and the assertion reports a false clean.
Listed in the design scope; manifest.yaml now declares provides.events with plugin.result and security_lens.failed, but config/event-schema.json was not touched to register these new event types.
Explicitly listed in the design scope and required by migration discipline (CLAUDE.md: tombstone in legacy/migrated/ when a keeper migrates), but no such file appears in the diff.
Listed in the design scope alongside other plugin documentation files; the plugin's public contract changed to v2 but the wiki file was not updated.

ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR is used verbatim in `mkdir -p` and as the parent of a written artifact with no path validation; an adversary who controls this environment variable (a system boundary per CLAUDE.md) can direct artifact writes to arbitrary filesystem locations via path traversal sequences.

_security_lens_interrupt_handler calls _security_lens_write_result which spawns a `date` subshell and pipes to atomic_write; running subprocess chains from inside a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler can mask the signal in child processes and prevent the outer pipeline from cleanly propagating the interrupt.

_sl_out_ref is set as an unscoped (global) variable before the TERM/INT trap and is never unset after `trap - TERM INT`; if the trap fires in a parent context after _security_lens_run_inner returns (e.g., due to a nested call or bash trap inheritance), the stale reference could cause the handler to overwrite an unintended artifact path.

The manifest declares `security_lens.failed` as an emitted event, but no `emit_event "security_lens.failed"` call appears anywhere in plugin.sh — all error paths emit only `plugin.result`, so any monitor or alert wired to `security_lens.failed` will never fire.

The rc=130 interrupt path writes a v2 artifact but emits no event to the bus; event-bus consumers watching for `plugin.result` or `security_lens.failed` cannot distinguish an interrupted review from a review that never ran.

`stub` is written as the JSON string `"false"` in `_security_lens_write_result`, whereas the pre-migration artifact carried the boolean `false`; consumers using `jq -e '.stub'` or `.data.stub` for truthiness checks will silently invert behavior (a string is truthy in jq, a boolean false is falsy).

`_security_lens_interrupt_handler` calls `_security_lens_write_result` (which spawns `jq` and `atomic_write`) inside a signal trap; if a second signal arrives during the handler, `atomic_write`'s temp-file rename may be abandoned and the artifact left corrupt or absent.

`_sl_out_ref` and `_sl_interrupted` are module-level (non-local) variables; if the shell sources plugin.sh more than once in the same process (e.g. test re-source after SPEC-10 shadow-and-restore), stale values from a prior interrupted run could suppress a required artifact write on the next run.

The cross-check guard now fires even when `ZBUILD_STATE_DIR` is explicitly set, meaning a corrupt but ultimately-ignored `ZBUILD_STATE_FILE` will abort the pipeline rather than being superseded by the authoritative state dir — the fail-closed behaviour is documented but widens blast radius for operators who set both variables in wrapper scripts.
